question.text: 'Koshy Credit AIF' closed with INR 1,000 crore in commitments. Drawdown 1 = 10% (management fees + setup), Drawdown 2 = 25% (Deal A), Drawdown 3 = 20% (Deal B). LP Ms. Nandini Rao's commitment is INR 30 crore. What is the CUMULATIVE capital Ms. Rao has contributed after all three drawdowns?

explanation.text: The Logic: Cumulative drawdown = 10% + 25% + 20% = 55%. Ms. Rao's called capital = 55% x INR 30 cr = INR 16.5 crore. The Trap: Option A is only drawdown 1. Option B is 35% error. Option D is full commitment. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B/C all test cumulative drawdown maths; XIX-C scenarios include fees-plus-deal drawdowns like this one. Manager's Pro-Tip: Initial drawdown typically covers setup + first year's management fee — disclose the first-drawdown composition in the PPM so LPs are not surprised by an 'expense-only' first call.
